question: Does a frozen predicted answer class suffice for first-exchange receiver decisions, or does within-class example-specific message variation materially change them?
status_at_registration: No new intervention results. Existing all1000 trajectories and their decoded-label tracking were inspected. This is not preregistration before observing development data.

predicted_classes.source: Argmax of each original native message classifier output from the frozen channel, not gold, receiver predictions, or post-intervention outputs.

arms.matched: Replay native other-agent packet, same private receiver context, author receiver-only terminal readout; exact predictions and all8 logits must match validated cross1 for both agents on all1000.
arms.within_class_0: Salt0 SHA256 ranking within the same frozen predicted class, one cyclic shift per class; no self-donor, bijective. Project original packets once, then permute the projected packets bit-for-bit.
arms.within_class_1: Identical rule with salt1. Sensitivity to donor choices, not independent replication.
arms.different_class: Sort predicted-class groups, SHA256 rank within groups with salt0, cyclically rotate concatenation by maximum class size; verify every donor has a different class, bijection and no self-donor. Positive control, not new causal-audit methodology.
arms.label_prefix: Class index selects one of8 existing teacher-prefix embeddings using the unchanged training template correct answer {label}. No gold, training, tuned prototype or continuous instance variation. Sender/classifier computation remains.

bootstrap.unit: target question conditional on fixed donor bank and plans
bootstrap.status: Descriptive only; not a formal population equivalence test; donor dependence and plan uncertainty omitted.

decision_rule.weak_positive_control: Stop bottleneck inference; diagnose whether intervention is actually influential.
decision_rule.all_tolerances_pass: Candidate first-exchange low-dimensional label relay; freeze held-out confirmation before opening926 official validation questions. No paper-level or full recurrent sufficiency claim.
decision_rule.within_class_pass_hard_prefix_fail: Discrete label-prefix teacher is insufficient, possibly calibration/geometry. Do not call the channel richly semantic.
decision_rule.within_class_fail: Residual message variation affects decisions; next discrimination is confidence/distribution versus task-specific semantic content. Do not automatically increase training or depth.

validity.replay: Both original receiver-only paths must match1000/1000 labels and every recorded label logit before new arms. Small-cohort pass is not accepted.
validity.fixed_environment: Model/data/checkpoint/config/vendor/torch/CUDA/flags and input tokens must match the validated baseline.

limitations: Development selection: no held-out inference or novelty proof.
Donor perturbations preserve class and packet marginal, not confidence or fine-grained content; failures are not semantic-content proofs.
Shared fixed8-entry codebook makes a class index at most3 bits, not a measured total-wire-cost or compute saving.
First-exchange sufficiency would not establish sufficiency throughout recurrent updates.
The task-specific label and prefix supervision are disclosed by the original authors.
Generic swaps/self controls and frozen-message anchoring are prior art or structural aliases, not contributions.

execution_policy.automatic_scheduler: No scheduled polling or automatic expansion is part of this fixed experiment.
execution_policy.on_failure: Save actual evidence; no unchanged retry, no threshold changes to manufacture success.
execution_policy.publication: Original code and aggregate evidence only; no question texts, private per-item files, tokens or author code.
